name: libdnet
why: A low-level networking library that is the key to ARP, raw packets and routing tables, but mostly plumbing unless you dig into the packets it exposes.

brief.what_it_is: libdnet is a C library that gives one simplified, portable interface to several low-level networking routines. Per its README, it covers network address manipulation, kernel arp(4) cache and route(4) table lookup and manipulation, network firewalling, network interface lookup and manipulation, IP tunnelling, and raw IP packet and Ethernet frame transmission. Programs call it with addresses, ARP and route entries, and raw packets as inputs, and get the kernel's networking state back or send frames out. The brew metadata lists two executables, dnet and dnet-config, but I did not see either named in the README.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a simplified, portable interface to low-level networking routines that differ from platform to platform. It does not spell out a longer motivation.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. The repository tree shows a src and include split, a man directory, a python directory, and both autotools (configure, Makefile.am) and CMake build files. I did not open those files, so I cannot describe the mechanism beyond the list of functions.
brief.install_notes: The README gives no install steps. The devel branch tree contains an INSTALL file, configure and configure.ac, CMakeLists.txt, and a libdnet.spec, so it builds from source with autotools or CMake. A dnet-config.in template suggests a config helper is generated at build time. I did not read these files, so treat the build details as unverified.
brief.standout: Few libraries put ARP cache, route table, firewall, interface, tunnel, and raw Ethernet and IP access behind one portable C API. That combination is the unusual part compared with using separate OS-specific tools or libraries for each.
brief.status: Unknown, leaning active. The GitHub page shows 835 commits, 187 stars, 68 forks, and a devel branch that the README calls the current work-in-progress with many fixes not yet merged to main. I did not see a release date or last-commit date, so I can't confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The README is very short and gives no usage examples or commands. The fixes that matter most are on the devel branch, not main, which the README says is kept for compatibility reasons. The brew scout note calls it mostly plumbing unless you work with the packets it exposes. Raw packet and ARP work usually needs root or elevated privileges, which I inferred from the subject matter and did not confirm in the README.
quotes: libdnet provides a simplified, portable interface to several low-level networking routines, including network address manipulation, kernel arp(4) cache and route(4) table lookup and manipulation, network firewalling, network interface lookup and manipulation, IP tunnelling, and raw IP packet and Ethernet frame transmission.

Before reporting an issue, please make sure you check the 'devel' branch to see if it's already fixed. This is the current WIP and contains already a lot of fixes, but for compatibilty reasons, it's not yet included in the main branch.
